answer: The summit multiplier is published, charged in thread, and orchard lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4076 identities would post 1538 proofs and burn roughly 22 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
